2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog
Psychology, Minor
Sponsoring department: Psychology
Basic psychological knowledge is essential for an understanding of modern culture. Discourse in the arts, media and politics is
infused with assumptions about the psyche. Educational debates hinge on differing theories of learning and cognition.
Medicine and science are increasingly aware of the impact of psychological factors on health and in the process of scientific
inquiry. Advertising and economic projections incorporate theories concerning human motivation. Understanding of human
cognitive processes is critical to the development of software technology and artificial intelligence systems.
Requirements for the Minor in Psychology
*Refer to Psychology Department section of this Catalog for a list of courses in each domain.
Note: Students must have a cumulative average of 2.5 based on all courses in the minor.
Students must take at least 20 credits or a minimum of 5 courses in Psychology, distributed as follows:
A. Research Methods: 4 Credits
PY 3010 - Research Design and Analysis I Credits: 4
PH 4670 - Biostatistics Credits: 4
SY 4520 - Research Methods I Credits: 4
B. One Foundations Course in Cognitive & Physiological: 4 Credits
C. One Foundations Course in Developmental, Clinical, or Social: 4 Credits
D. One Foundations Course in Diversity & Social Justice: 4 Credits
E. One 4000‑level Psych Elective: 4 Credits
(Residency Requirement)
